c74object.name: syncSuite.netscan
c74object.digest: Reports your machine's own IP/mask, and discovers live devices on a subnet via a ping sweep.
c74object.description: Use it to find your own IPv4 address(es) and netmask(s), and to discover which devices answer on a given subnet.

objarg.name: ip
objarg.digest: Subnet IP to scan on load
objarg.description: Together with "mask", runs a scan of this subnet as soon as the patcher containing this object finishes loading, equivalent to sending "scan <ip> <mask>". Optional; omit both arguments to scan nothing automatically.

objarg.name: mask
objarg.digest: Subnet mask to scan on load
objarg.description: See "ip". Both arguments must be given together, e.g. "syncSuite.netscan 192.168.0.1 255.255.255.0".

inlet.digest: Commands controlling the underlying Node process and network requests
inlet.description: Accepts "start", "stop", "myip", "myip all", "scan", "scan <ip> <mask>", and "ping <ip>". See the Messages section for the full list.

outlet.description: Outputs "<iface> <ip> <mask>" for each active non-internal IPv4 interface — more than one message if you're connected to more than one network at once. After "myip all", each message additionally ends with "internal" or "external", and internal/loopback interfaces are included too.

For "scan", outputs "<iface> <host1> <host2> ..." listing every device that answered the ping sweep on that subnet (or "<iface> none" if nobody answered). Sending "scan" with no arguments produces one such message per active interface, scanning each interface's own subnet in turn. For "ping", outputs "<ip> <0|1>" — 1 if that host answered, 0 if it didn't.

outlet.digest: Bangs once a "myip"/"scan"/"ping" request finishes reporting
outlet.description: Fires right after outlet 0 (for "myip"/"myip all") or outlet 1 (for each "scan" or "ping" report) finishes sending its results — useful as a "done" signal to sequence further processing.

method.name: start
method.description: Launches the Node script backing this object. Not normally needed — the script starts automatically the first time it's needed — but useful after "stop", or to force a restart.

method.name: stop
method.description: Shuts down the running Node script. Any scan in progress is abandoned without reporting.

method.name: myip
method.digest: Reports this machine's own IPv4 address(es) and netmask(s)
method.description: Reports every active non-internal IPv4 interface on outlet 0, one message per interface, then bangs outlet 2. If you're on more than one network at once, you get more than one message — nothing is dropped.

method.name: myip
method.digest: Reports every IPv4 interface, including internal/loopback
method.description: Sent as "myip all". Same as plain "myip", but also includes internal/loopback interfaces, and tags each reported message "internal" or "external" at the end.

method.name: scan
method.digest: Discovers live devices on a subnet via a ping sweep
method.description: Sent as "scan <ip> <mask>" (e.g. "scan 192.168.0.1 255.255.255.0"), pings every host in that subnet and reports which ones answered on outlet 1, then bangs outlet 2. Sent as bare "scan" with no arguments, scans every currently active interface's own subnet in turn, one report + bang per interface. A device answering the ping means it exists on the network — it does not by itself mean any particular UDP or TCP port on that device is reachable.

method.name: ping
method.description: Sent as "ping <ip>" (e.g. "ping 192.168.0.12"). Pings just that one host and reports "<ip> <0|1>" on outlet 1 — 1 if it answered, 0 if it didn't — then bangs outlet 2.
